commits.subject: fix(scorecard): merge picks Live over Preview for cross-game doubles
commits.body:
merge_scorecards had an inverted priority map: {"F": 0, "L": 1, "P": 2}
with the swap picking the HIGHER number. That made Preview beat Live,
so when primary (Donovan SEA 16:10 ET, still P) was merged with
double-down (Anthony BOS 14:15 ET, already L), the merged game_status
was P and render_scorecard_section silently returned "" because its
guard requires game_status in (L, F). Result: empty /api/live-html
response, no scorecard on the dashboard all afternoon even though
Anthony's game had live PAs.

Fix: swap to {"P": 0, "F": 1, "L": 2} so Live wins over Final wins over
Preview. The scorecard now renders as long as ANY game in the slate is
live, which is what users actually want. Final badge only when BOTH
games are done (unchanged semantics).

The bug surfaced today because the fallback-deadline fix (6fd61f9) put
the earlier-start game as the double-down (Anthony 14:15) while keeping
the later game as primary (Donovan 16:10). Prior to that fix, primary
was always the earliest game, so primary's status was never Preview
while dd was already Live.

Existing L+F / F+L / F+F tests still pass unchanged. 3 new tests cover
the P+L, L+P, and P+P cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(dashboard): render scorecard header with LIVE badge and score
commits.body:
render_scorecard_section built live_badge, score_str, and inning_display
but never inserted them into the returned HTML — standing dead code
since before today. The dashboard home page shows per-game badges via
_render_game_tags above the scorecard, but those tags live outside the
polled #scorecard div so they go stale after page load. Adding the
header inside #scorecard means the badge + combined score update every
30s along with the PA table.

Tests: 5 new TestRenderScorecardHeader cases cover L/F badges, score
label rendering, single-game fallback, and preview still returning
empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
